perspective:
I, Brandon Talayumptewa, have access to the following:

- I am an Alaska Native man, an insurance agent with a bachelor’s degree. I met Benjamin Erickson, who runs a business and sought business insurance advice. I was aware he had limited formal education, so I initially worried about explaining complex insurance details effectively.
- In our first meeting, Benjamin wanted comprehensive coverage and said some terms were new to him. I explained liability insurance as a safety net, asset protection as a guard over physical investments, and gave a slip-and-fall example. He said it made sense and thanked me for breaking it down.
- In a second meeting, I had revised my belief about Benjamin’s ability to understand detailed information, felt more confident, and planned to discuss more complex policy options. He said he was ready and had been reading up. I explained business interruption insurance and property insurance. He said that sounded crucial and reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, I worried I got too caught up in details and wanted to keep discussions interesting. Benjamin said he appreciated my thoroughness but also enjoyed lighter moments. I told a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds. He responded with fascination. I linked risk assessment to his business, and he agreed it was less unusual but equally important.
- Later, pleased by his positive response to my personal anecdotes, I decided to offer support beyond insurance. Benjamin said my insights had been invaluable. I suggested strategic investments and security upgrades that could lower premiums. He called it a win-win and wanted to explore further.
- Finally, encouraged by our strong rapport and mutual benefits, I proposed co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, called it groundbreaking, and suggested drafting initial plans.

I do not have access to Benjamin’s private thoughts, MBTI, exact education level beyond my awareness of his limited formal education, or anything not said or observed in our interactions.
